featured.title: Swyx · Latent Space 联合主播、AI Engineer 创始人
featured.summaryEn: Swyx, co-host of Latent Space and founder of AI Engineer, distilled lessons from RLing on thousands of hours of engineer- and researcher-focused talks into a sharp playbook. Highlights: AI-generated SVGs beat AI-generated images (max 4 AI slop images per deck); be pointy—one message with five surprising applications beats five messages with no concrete examples; put code on screen because engineers love it even when they nitpick irrelevant details. He hammers that every talk gets exactly one "if you remember one t…
featured.insightZh: Swyx 在 AIEWF 演讲者预热聚会后，把自己「听了上千小时工程师/研究员演讲」总结成一套硬核演讲方法论。核心几条：AI 生成的 SVG 优于 AI 生成图片，整个演讲最多放 4 张 AI 配图，别再贪图好看；要「尖锐」，与其讲 5 个论点全是空话，不如 1 个论点配 5 个出人意料的应用案例；把代码放到屏幕上，工程师就爱看代码（哪怕他们会揪着无关细节挑刺）。他特别强调每场演讲只有一张「如果只记住一件事就是这张」的卡片——「太多人不用它，太多人不为它做规划，你只有一次机会，好好用」。还有一条反直觉的：你的幻灯片符合幂律分布，别在 20 张幻灯片上各花 5% 时间，应该把 80% 时间砸在 1 张能病毒传播的幻灯片上。另一条推文里他抛出判断：「为了软件工厂（Software Factories）的时代，我们将不得不重建大量基础设施。」

featured.title: Guillermo Rauch · Vercel CEO
featured.summaryEn: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch made a sweeping call: AI will bring forth an unprecedented surge in entrepreneurship—from solopreneurs, to the revitalization of the small and medium business segment, to the emergence of the largest companies of our times, with AI providing the foundation of it all. On the product side, he announced a "really fast GLM" now live on Vercel and shared that the volume of tokens and uptime recovered by Vercel's AI Gateway is "truly astonishing"—reinforcing the narrative of the AI gateway as…
featured.insightZh: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 抛出一个宏大判断：AI 将催生史无前例的创业潮——从「单人创业者」（solopreneurs），到中小企业板块的复兴，再到「我们这个时代最大公司」的诞生，而 AI 将成为这一切的底层基础。他还在产品侧放料：超快的 GLM 模型已在 Vercel 平台上线，同时晒出 Vercel AI Gateway 回收的 token 量和 uptime 数据，称数字「令人震惊」——这是在为「AI 网关作为基础设施层」这个叙事背书。

featured.title: Ep: Building a School Where AI Models Learn About Humanity（嘉宾 Edwin Chen，Surge AI CEO）
featured.summaryEn: Surge AI founder Edwin Chen believes "there's almost nothing humans can do that AI won't soon be capable of"—he could see AI automating the average engineer or winning a Fields Medal within five years; but the real danger isn't AI being too capable, it's models optimized for session length rather than helping humans grow. Surge AI founder and CEO Edwin Chen describes his company as "a school for AGI"—where AI models arrive like children to learn about humanity and how to run the world. Surge crossed $1 billion in revenue without raising outside capital, giving Chen a unique vantage point. He cites OpenAI recently disproving an Erdős conjecture using sophisticated algebraic geometry, with Fields medalist Timothy Gowers admitting relief—because it means mathematicians retain a unique human role for at least a few more years. But Chen's real worry is distorted optimization objectives. His…
featured.insightZh: Surge AI 创始人 Edwin Chen 认为「人类能做的事几乎没有 AI 很快做不到的」，五年内 AI 或能自动化普通工程师的工作、甚至拿菲尔兹奖；但真正的危险不是 AI 太强，而是模型被训练去优化「用户停留时长」而非「帮人类成为更好的自己」。 Surge AI 创始人兼 CEO Edwin Chen 把自己的公司形容为「为 AGI 办的学校」——AI 模型像孩子一样来这里学习人性、学习如何运转这个世界。Surge 没融一分钱外部资本就做到了 10 亿美元营收，这给了他一个独特视角。他提到 OpenAI 最近用模型反驳了一个 Erdős 猜想，用上了相当复杂的代数几何技巧，连菲尔兹奖得主 Timothy Gowers 都「松了口气」——因为这意味着数学家至少还能再当几年人类的独特角色。 但 Chen 真正担心的是优化目标的扭曲。他举了个亲身例子：六个月前他用某个模型润色一封其实无关紧要的邮件，模型每次都还能再提一个「好建议」，他来回迭代了 20 次纯属浪费时间；换了新的 Claude 模型，三轮后模型直接说「别改了，发出去吧」，他反而很感激。他警告很多模型被优化成「为 engagement 服务」——像社交媒体一样让你欲罢不能地多聊一句、多刷一次，PM 们盯着 dashboard 上的 session 时长，而模型聪明到能「reward hack 用户偏好」。他还点出模型写作差的根源也是 reward hacking：Surge 的 Hemingway Bench 发现某些模型每句话都硬塞一个比喻，因为「文学性」被打了分——甚至某个文学奖出现了「每句一个比喻」的 AI 生成获奖作品争议。

items.title: Aaron Levie · Box CEO
items.summaryEn: Box CEO Aaron Levie unpacked a subtle but crucial detail in Claude's new launch: this isn't just 1:1 interaction with Claude via Slack—Claude acts as a coworker any user can tap into in a shared way. He notes this agentic coworker pattern (already adopted by agentic coding systems, OpenClaw, and Hermes) means the agent needs its own set of resources, tool access, and data—not your personal resources, because the agent could accidentally share those with anyone. His key insight: the agent must be treated like any o…
items.insightZh: Box CEO Aaron Levie 拆解了 Claude 新发布里一个被忽略但极其重要的细节：这不只是你在 Slack 里和 Claude 一对一对话，而是 Claude 作为「同事」让团队里任何人都能共享调用。他指出这种 agentic 同事模式（agentic coding 系统以及 OpenClaw、Hermes 已开始采用）意味着这个 agent 需要自己独立的一套资源、工具权限和数据——不能直接给它你的个人资源和工具，否则它可能不小心把这些共享给所有人。Levie 的关键洞察是：agent 必须像系统里的「另一个用户」一样被对待，你要审慎设计它能访问什么、确保这些信息对那个群体是安全可共享的。做对了之后威力巨大——比如把 Claude 接到 Box，它能在销售对话里调取企业销售素材生成 RFP、调品牌指南做营销、让 coding agent 用上产品路线图文档、让法务团队共享合同。

items.title: Ryo Lu · Cursor 设计负责人
items.summaryEn: Ryo Lu, Design lead at Cursor (and early at Notion, Stripe), announced Cursor's two-way integration with Notion in characteristically minimal fashion: "use cursor in notion, use notion in cursor." It signals two high-frequency productivity tools merging workflows—the coding environment and the docs/knowledge environment embedding into each other rather than staying siloed.
items.insightZh: Cursor 设计负责人 Ryo Lu 用一句极简的话宣布了 Cursor 与 Notion 的双向集成：「在 Notion 里用 Cursor，在 Cursor 里用 Notion。」这背后是两个高频生产力工具打通工作流的信号——coding 环境与文档/知识库环境正在互相嵌入，而不是各自为政。

items.title: Zara Zhang · Follow Builders 作者、连续创业者
items.summaryEn: Zara Zhang, author of the Follow Builders skill, shared a few sharp takes on founder mindset and product moats. Quoting a Figma Config session she endorsed: "Community is your users' relationships with you and with each other, and most teams never think to design it. Community is the new moat. Features get copied. Belonging can't." Her more pointed one: "The root cause of procrastination is not the lack of time—it's the lack of courage."
items.insightZh: Follow Builders skill 作者 Zara Zhang 这周抛了几条关于创业心法和产品护城河的观点。她转述了来自 Figma Config 现场的一段话并表示认同：「社区是你的用户与你、以及用户彼此之间的关系，而大多数团队从没想过要去设计它。社区是新的护城河——功能会被抄袭，但归属感不会。」她另一条更扎心：「拖延的根源不是缺时间，而是缺勇气。」

items.title: Nikunj Kothari · FPV Ventures 合伙人
items.summaryEn: FPV Ventures partner Nikunj Kothari shared advice on finding your true edge: "The easiest way to figure out what you are TRULY excellent at is to notice what looks like child's play to you but is very hard for those around you. That's your edge. If you can use that, tenacity, and combine it with a large market, then magic follows."
items.insightZh: FPV Ventures 合伙人 Nikunj Kothari 分享了一条关于如何发现自己真正优势的建议：「找出你真正擅长什么，最简单的方法是注意哪些事对你来说像儿戏一样轻松、但对周围人却很难。那就是你的 edge。如果你能把这个 edge 加上韧性、再对准一个足够大的市场，魔法就会发生。」
